text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Banking expert sees possibility of a merger between Bank Austria and Creditanstalt within the year, even though the coalition agreed that Creditanstalt would remain independent for the next five years.
- More than 300,000 Austrians were unemployed in January -- the highest number since the 1950s.
- Four members of the provincial Carinthian parliament have stepped down after a scandal concerning faked signatures.
- Five companies have so far shown interest in Austria's third mobile phone licence. A decision is expected in autumn.
- BMW is thinking about plans to create a world-wide research and development centre in Austria.
- A majority of Austrians would accept more flexible work hours, study shows.
- Neutrality and the schilling are losing importance for Austrians, while a restriction of foreign workers is becoming more important, study shows.

- The post's mobile phone company Mobilkom is planning the expansion of its network at a cost of one billion schillings. The decision on which company will receive the order is expected by the end of February.
- Styria is examining subsidies to papermaker KNP Leykam, as the firm has announced cutting 500 jobs.
- The number of unemployed is at a record high level and the forecast is not improving.
- Raiffeisen Laenderbank will take over a 49 percent stake in Upper Austria's Hypo bank.
- BMW is criticising high labour costs in Austria, saying a new motor engineering plant will be made in England.
